page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of RAM, providing 1.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 50 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance scales moderately, with stress-ng multi-core and static web serving throughput landing in the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark physics tests fall into the weak tier. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the poor tier, although raw memory bandwidth tests for small cached blocks remain average.

Given its shared CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic utility scripting. However, it is not recommended for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized multi-threaded applications due to its constrained 2.0 GB RAM capacity and weak multi-threaded scaling.
